answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or earn fees. Rewards accrue only to identities that complete independently verified work, while proven fraud burns the locked stake. Splitting one actor into a thousand accounts then multiplies the capital tied up without multiplying useful output. A ledge-side ferrous assay or a willow survey still needs real evidence; names alone cannot mint rewards. The attacker pays an opportunity cost on every stake and risks losing it.
